University of Arkansas


  


Doctoral research · Developing now


Understanding performance across environments
Within FernandesLAB, my doctoral research is developing around how genotypes respond differently across environments and how the spatial structure of environments can improve the interpretation and prediction of those responses. Detailed project pages, methods, results, and visualizations will be added as the work progresses.


01

Genotype × Environment Interactions
Studying how genetic differences and environmental conditions combine to influence observed traits and performance.



02

Spatial Analysis of Genotype × Environment Interactions
Investigating spatial patterns and environmental relationships that can strengthen genotype-by-environment analysis and prediction.

title: Personality
text:
Assessment results




Kirton Adaption–Innovation Inventory
The KAI Inventory focuses on preferred problem-solving style—especially how a person approaches structure and change. It does not measure intelligence, ability, or creativity level.




My result


84total score



40OriginalitySufficiency of Originality


8EfficiencyMethodology


36StructureRule/Group Conformity





What I take from this result
My score is most useful as a prompt for understanding how I work with other people. I tend to combine disciplined execution with independent analysis: I appreciate structure when it improves clarity, but I am comfortable revisiting assumptions and proposing a different route when the evidence supports it.
The three component scores describe different aspects of that preference. They should be interpreted together and in context, rather than as separate measures of performance.

title: Personality
text:
The four Keirsey temperaments
Keirsey organizes 16 personality types into four broad temperaments. The compact map below makes the relationship between each temperament and its four types easier to scan.



SP


Artisan
Action-oriented, adaptable, and pragmatic.

ESTP Promoter ISTP Crafter ESFP Performer ISFP Composer





SJ


Guardian
Dependable, organized, and attentive to responsibility.

ESTJ Supervisor My result ISTJ Inspector ESFJ Provider ISFJ Protector





NF


Idealist
People-centered, empathetic, and guided by possibilities.

ENFJ Teacher INFJ Counselor ENFP Champion INFP Healer





NT


Rational
Strategic, analytical, and oriented toward systems and competence.

ENTJ Fieldmarshal My result INTJ Mastermind ENTP Inventor INTP Architect






Two results, one useful pattern
Across assessments, my reported types have been ENTJ and ESTJ. In Keirsey’s framework, these sit in different temperaments—Rational and Guardian—but share an emphasis on outward engagement, analytical decision-making, and organized action.
Rather than choosing one label, I use both results as a practical reflection of how context can bring different aspects of my working style to the foreground.

title: Teaching
text:
Learning objectives
The materials in this section are designed to help learners:

Understand important statistical and analytical concepts.
Connect mathematical ideas with practical applications.
Apply methods using reproducible computational workflows.
Interpret results carefully and communicate conclusions clearly.
Build the confidence needed to explore more advanced topics independently.

title: Teaching
text:

Prerequisites depend on the course or tutorial. Each teaching page will identify the background knowledge required before beginning.
When computation is involved, materials may use:

R and RStudio for statistical analysis
Quarto for reproducible documents and presentations
Course-specific R packages and datasets

Installation instructions and required software will be listed on the relevant page.
